title: Saying look at me to show a skill is listed at 30 months
summary: Most children show what they can do by saying look at me by about 30 months, CDC says.
body: CDC's 30-month social milestones include showing you what she can do by saying look at me. The phrase pulls a partner's attention onto the child's own act. Most means 75 percent or more, so the line is not a vocabulary test and not a rule about one sentence. The materials are not a substitute for validated screening. The wording is the US checklist's example.

sources.title: Learn the Signs. Act Early. milestone page
sources.author: CDC
sources.note: Supports the 30-month social milestone about saying look at me to show what she can do. US federal page, public domain. Paraphrased, not quoted.
